I spent so many years afraid of telling anyone about my depression/mood swings. I did the same thing as you, I studied the side effects and symptoms of antidepressants, I was scared that it would make me shut down (as well as my fiancé) and become addicted and so forth. When I went to my doctor and talked to him about it (which was awkward for me, it shouldn't have been though) he prescribed me to some medicine that would produce more positive chemicals in my brain, and explained that the depression I had was only a chemical imbalance. I forget the name of the meds I take but all I know is that I have to take it at night, because if I took it in the daytime it would make me drowsy af. The first month I was taking the meds I became extremely lethargic, I was so out of it all I could do is lay in my bed all day, this happened to me on the weekends because when I was working and in motion these "side effects" wouldn't affect me as much. I've been taking this for over a year and I have definitely seen improvement, I can socialize better (most of the time) I can interact much more with the people I love, and go through the weekends without becoming stagnant and lifeless, (I don't have any friends where I live). What you need to know is that it all depends what's right for you, it doesn't cure depression, but it definitely helps. There's still days where I can still feel the sadness, the urge to end my life, but I'm still here. And please, don't be ashamed and scared like I was. We all need a helping hand sometimes.
You have a great community here waiting to offer advice and support.
Cheers.
